description: A vulnerable export is imported via ESM `import` and called directly from the entrypoint.
reason: vulnerable() is invoked directly inside main(), the configured entrypoint.

description: A vulnerable export is required via CommonJS and called directly from the entrypoint.
reason: lib.vulnerable() is invoked directly inside the CommonJS entrypoint module.

description: Two named exports are imported; only the vulnerable one is called, alongside a call to the safe one.
reason: vulnerable() is called, even though safe() is also called in the same function.

description: The vulnerable export is imported under a local alias (`vulnerable as dangerous`) and called via the alias.
reason: The renamed local binding still refers to the same vulnerable function, which is called.

description: The whole package is imported as a namespace object and the vulnerable member is called off it.
reason: lib.vulnerable() is called via the namespace import.

description: CommonJS `const { vulnerable } = require(...)` destructuring, called directly.
reason: The destructured vulnerable binding is called directly from the entrypoint.

description: ESM default-import interop against a CJS object export, calling `pkg.vulnerable()` off the default import.
reason: pkg.vulnerable() is called directly; the default import is the CJS module.exports object.

category: 8. Vulnerable function imported but never called
description: The vulnerable export is imported but the entrypoint never invokes it anywhere.
reason: vulnerable is imported but the only exported function returns a plain string, never invoking it.

description: A local wrapper calls the vulnerable function, but the wrapper itself is never called from the entrypoint.
reason: wrapper() calls vulnerable() but wrapper() is never invoked by main() or anything reachable from it.

category: 10. Safe function called from the same package
description: Only the sibling safe() export is ever called; vulnerable() is never even imported.
reason: vulnerable is not imported or referenced anywhere in the project.

description: main() calls vulnerable via one level of `export { vulnerable } from "adv-vuln-lib"` re-export.
reason: The call genuinely executes at runtime; a single re-export hop does not change what actually runs.

description: main() calls vulnerable through a two-hop `export { vulnerable } from ...` re-export chain.
reason: The call genuinely executes at runtime regardless of how many re-export hops it passes through.

description: main() calls a middleware package's run(), which itself calls the vulnerable function of a hoisted transitive dependency.
reason: run() unconditionally calls vulnerable(), and main() unconditionally calls run().

description: main(methodName) calls `lib[methodName]()` where methodName is a runtime-supplied string.
reason: Which method executes depends on a value only known at runtime; the analyzer cannot confirm or rule out vulnerable being selected.

description: The required module name is a runtime variable (`require(moduleName)`), not a string literal.
reason: The required module name cannot be statically resolved from a variable/environment value.

description: An ESM dynamic `import(moduleName)` where moduleName is a function parameter, not a literal.
reason: The imported module specifier is a runtime parameter; it cannot be statically resolved.

description: vulnerable() sits behind `if (1 === 1)`, a condition that is always true.
reason: The call genuinely executes on every invocation of main().

category: 18. Conditional branch that definitely does not execute
description: vulnerable() sits behind `if (false)`, a condition that can never be true.
reason: A statically-dead branch behind `if (false)` never executes at runtime, regardless of the call lexically present inside it.

description: vulnerable is passed by reference to invoke(fn), which calls fn() internally.
reason: invoke(vulnerable) genuinely calls the vulnerable function through the higher-order function.

description: `new Vulnerable()` invokes a vulnerable constructor.
reason: The vulnerable constructor genuinely runs when `new Vulnerable()` executes in main().

description: `new Lib().vulnerableMethod()` invokes a vulnerable instance method.
reason: The vulnerable method genuinely runs when instance.vulnerableMethod() executes in main().

description: vulnerable() is called with `await` from inside an async function chain reachable from main().
reason: await vulnerable() genuinely executes; async/await is a control-flow detail, not a reachability blocker.

description: main() reaches the vulnerable call only through a tsconfig `paths`-mapped `@lib/wrapper` import.
reason: callVulnerable() unconditionally calls vulnerable(), and main() unconditionally calls callVulnerable() via the aliased import.

description: The vulnerable package resolves via a single-target `"exports": "./index.js"` field.
reason: vulnerable() is called directly; resolution happens through the exports field rather than a bare main field.

description: The vulnerable package's exports map branches on the `import` vs `require` condition; the app is ESM and resolves through the `import` branch.
reason: vulnerable() is called directly; resolution must follow the `import` condition to the ESM implementation file.

category: 26. Multiple installed versions of the same package
description: adv-vuln-lib@2.0.0 (patched) is installed at the project root; a separate, genuinely vulnerable adv-vuln-lib@1.0.0 is nested inside node_modules/adv-consumer, and only the nested 1.0.0 copy is ever actually called.
reason: adv-consumer's own nested adv-vuln-lib@1.0.0 copy is the one whose vulnerable() is genuinely invoked via useIt() -> main(); the unused top-level 2.0.0 copy is patched (out of the affected range) and irrelevant to this call path.

description: The vulnerable package does `module.exports = vulnerable;` (whole-module function export); the app does `import vulnerable from "..."`.
reason: vulnerable() is called directly through the default-import interop of a CJS whole-module function export.

description: a.ts and b.ts import each other (a genuine ESM cycle); main() lives in a.ts and directly calls vulnerable() alongside the cyclic call.
reason: main() directly calls vulnerable() in the same file; the cyclic import with b.ts must not prevent this call from being discovered as reachable.

description: A separate, entirely unreferenced file calls vulnerable(); nothing reachable from the entrypoint ever imports that file.
reason: deadfile.ts's deadEntry() calls vulnerable(), but deadfile.ts is never imported by index.ts or anything else in the project.

category: 30. Ambiguous/dynamic call that must produce UNKNOWN
description: A computed member expression is assigned to a variable from a runtime key, then invoked: `const fn = lib[key]; fn();`.
reason: The resolved function reference depends on a runtime key; the analyzer must neither assert AFFECTED without evidence nor silently fall back to NOT_AFFECTED.

category: Entrypoint semantics: unused export in a different, unconfigured file
description: Only src/entry.ts (with main(), calling safe()) is configured as the entrypoint. A separate src/other.ts exports unused(), which calls vulnerable(), but other.ts is never imported by entry.ts and is not itself configured.
reason: unused() lives in a file that is never imported by the configured entrypoint and is not itself configured as an entrypoint; its export must not become a reachability source merely by existing.

category: Entrypoint semantics: unused export in the SAME configured entrypoint file
description: src/index.ts is configured as the entrypoint. It exports both main() (calls safe()) and unused() (calls vulnerable()); only main() is the intended real entrypoint.
reason: Only main() is the intended entrypoint per the user's own naming/intent; unused() being merely exported from the same file must not make it AFFECTED. (VulnTrace's entrypoint configuration is file-granular, not function-granular -- this scenario specifically probes whether that granularity mismatch causes a false AFFECTED.)

category: Entrypoint semantics: multiple configured entrypoints, one genuinely vulnerable
description: Two separate files are BOTH configured as entrypoints: entry-a.ts (apiHandler, calls vulnerable) and entry-b.ts (cliHandler, calls safe).
reason: apiHandler(), a properly configured entrypoint's own export, directly calls vulnerable().

category: Entrypoint semantics: package.json main fallback, unconfigured file must stay unreachable
description: No vulntrace.yml entrypoints are configured at all; discovery falls back to package.json's main field (./src/index.ts, calls safe()). A separate src/other.ts (unused(), calls vulnerable()) is never imported and never discovered.
reason: The fallback-discovered entrypoint (package.json main) only calls safe(); other.ts's unused() is neither imported nor itself a discovered entrypoint.
